record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Are any of the Borel τ-cover properties S1(BT, BΓ), S1(BT, BT), S1(BT, BΩ), S1(BT, B), Sfin(BT, BT), or Sfin(BT, BΩ) inherited by all subsets?

evidence.quote: Are any of the properties S1(BT, BΓ), S1(BT, BT), S1(BT, BΩ), S1(BT, B), Sfin(BT, BT), or Sfin(BT, BΩ), hereditary?

artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of the heredity question for these six Borel τ-cover selection properties. The combinatorics of Borel τ-covers has been studied (e.g., Scheepers–Tsaban, "The combinatorics of Borel covers"; further works on τ-cover combinatorics), and while many heredity questions for open-cover analogues have been settled, no source found establishes or refutes heredity for the listed Borel τ-cover properties. Status appears to remain open or unresolved in the accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Several comments about the combinatorics of tau-covers
status_evidence.snippet: Combinatorics of selection hypotheses involving tau-covers is sensitive to the selection operator used.
status_evidence.claim: Tau-cover selection principles remain a subject of active investigation without a comprehensive heredity resolution.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Many heredity questions for selection principles involving tau-covers are listed among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Heredity for Borel τ-cover selection principles is listed as an open direction.
